sentences.text: The genus name Pegomastax translates to "strong jaw" in Greek, while the species name indicates its African origin.
The only known material consists of a partial skull with a well-preserved lower jaw, including a postorbital bone, both jaw bones, and a predentary.
This animal measured no more than 60 centimeters from head to tail, with a skull length of 73 millimeters.
It possessed a robust lower jaw featuring a short beak.
Unlike its relatives, Pegomastax possessed a straight caniniform tooth at the front of its jaw.
Like most other heterodontosaurids, it had an enlarged canine-like tooth at the beginning of its lower jaw row, which may have served a defensive function.
The only known specimen was discovered during a 1966–1967 expedition in South Africa but was not formally described until 2012 by Paul Sereno.
The holotype specimen, accession number SAM-PK-K10488, was found at the Voyizane locality in the Transkei District within rocks from the upper Elliot Formation.
Wear patterns on its teeth suggest Pegomastax was herbivorous, likely eating tougher plants than its relatives that lacked a canine tooth.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Pegomastax as a derived heterodontosaurid in the subfamily Heterodontosaurinae, with the South American taxon Manidens identified as its closest relative.
Pegomastax lived during the earliest Jurassic, specifically the Hettangian and Sinemurian epochs, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago.
Some 2017 phylogenetic analyses alternatively resolve Pegomastax as the sister taxon to a group containing Heterodontosaurus and Lycorhinus.
Researchers have noted that the internal relationships within Heterodontosauridae are weakly supported and require further investigation.
There is debate regarding the function of heterodontosaurid canines, with suggestions ranging from omnivory and defense to processing tough, fibrous vegetation.
Norman et al. (2011) suggested that heterodontosaurid canines were unlikely used for display or vegetation processing due to a lack of wear and evidence for sexual variation.
